International Cheese Federation: Industry News and Member Updates
This page from the International Cheese Federation provides a chronological listing of recent news articles, educational opportunities, member spotlights, and event announcements. Key topics include milk price fluctuations and financial margins, food safety regulations and training, milk supply and cheese demand trends, professional certifications like the Certified Cheese Professional (CCP), judging standards, and advocacy for small producers.

Milk prices recover, margins stay tight

Allergen controls, and the deadline that’s closer than it looks

Twenty years in cheese, most of them teaching food safety 

 

Gwen Whitfield has spent two decades in cheese and now runs her own food-safety training practice. We asked her what changed her mind about teaching over making.

Fewer cows, a steady case 

 

National milk cow numbers keep drifting down while cheese demand holds steady. We look at what a slow-growth spring means for members on both sides of the vat.

The CCP: what it actually covers, and who it’s for

Margins firm up, but keep an eye on the fall 

 

Milk prices are finally climbing out of a two-year trough, but an international trade dispute working its way through arbitration could reshape the cheese case before the year is out.

What a small-producer exemption actually covers 

 

Members keep asking whether their creamery qualifies for a food-safety exemption. The honest answer is it’s narrower than the rumor, and here’s what we’re pushing the regulator to clarify.

What the herd decides before you do
